title: Strip quotes from quoted require paths in goModRequirePaths

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Go allows a quoted module path in `go.mod`, such as `require "quoted.example/q" v1.0.0`, in both the one-line form and inside a `require (` block. `goModRequirePaths` in `internal/engine/gomodimports.go` appends the first field as it is (lines 61 and 72), so the quotes stay in the path. `goModuleImportsSection` then lists it as `` - `"quoted.example/q"` `` in the reviewer brief. A probe test would be told to import a path with quotes in it. Such paths are rare and S589's spec did not cover them (raised by the gate in round 1 of ork run ork-20261125-224829-7bd0).

The fix unquotes a require path with the standard library's `strconv.Unquote`, which accepts both the interpreted (`"..."`) and the raw (`` `...` ``) Go string forms. The dedupe step already runs after the paths are collected, so a quoted and an unquoted spelling of one path collapse into a single entry.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `TestGoModRequirePathsStripsQuotes`: directly calls goModRequirePaths with interpreted-quoted paths in a require block and one-line require, a raw-quoted path, and an unquoted duplicate. Assert unquoted paths in file order without duplicates or quote characters. Fails before implementation because quotes remain.
- `TestGoModRequirePathsKeepsUnparsableQuotedField`: directly calls goModRequirePaths with an unterminated quoted field and ordinary paths. Assert the invalid field and other paths remain unchanged. This fallback guard passes before implementation; mutation-check it after implementation.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/engine/gomodimports_test.go`, add the two tests above as direct calls to `goModRequirePaths` (same package `engine`), written first and shown failing for the first test.
2. In `internal/engine/gomodimports.go`, add `"strconv"` to the imports.
3. Add a small helper `unquoteModPath(field string) string` that returns `strconv.Unquote(field)` when it succeeds and `field` unchanged when it returns an error. An unquoted field also fails `Unquote`, so it passes through unchanged.
4. In `goModRequirePaths`, wrap both appends with the helper: `paths = append(paths, unquoteModPath(fields[0]))` at the block-line case and `paths = append(paths, unquoteModPath(fields[1]))` at the one-line case. Leave the dedupe step as it is, so it sees the unquoted paths.
5. Extend the doc comment of `goModRequirePaths` with one sentence: a quoted path is listed without its quotes.
6. Run the checks below.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -run TestGoModRequirePathsStripsQuotes ./internal/engine` passes. It fails before the change, with the quotes in the returned paths.
- `go test -run TestGoModRequirePathsKeepsUnparsableQuotedField ./internal/engine` passes.
- `go test -run TestGoModuleImportsSectionListsRequirePaths ./internal/engine` still passes, so the unquoted listing is unchanged.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- `go vet ./...` prints nothing.
- `gofmt -l ./internal/engine` prints nothing.
